sanskrit: tvam anāsādya tān bāṇān phalgunasya vigarjasi pārthasāyakaviddhasya durlabhaṃ garjitaṃ bhavet
english: You roar because you have not yet met the arrows of Phalguna; once you are pierced by Pārtha's shafts, your roaring will be hard to come by.

sanskrit: bāhubhiḥ kṣatriyāḥ śūrā vāgbhiḥ śūrā dvijātayaḥ dhanuṣā phalgunaḥ śūraḥ karṇaḥ śūro manorathaiḥ
english: Kṣatriyas are valiant with their arms, the twice-born are valiant with their words; Phalguna is valiant with his bow, but Karṇa is valiant only in his daydreams.

sanskrit: evaṃ paruṣitas tena tadā śāradvatena saḥ karṇaḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kṛpaṃ vākyam athābravīt
english: Thus harshly upbraided by Śāradvata, Karṇa, the foremost of those who strike, then spoke these words to Kṛpa.

sanskrit: śūrā garjanti satataṃ prāvṛṣīva balāhakāḥ phalaṃ cāśu prayacchanti bījam uptam ṛtāv iva
english: Heroes ever roar, like the storm clouds in the rains; and swiftly they yield their fruit, as seed sown in its season.

sanskrit: doṣam atra na paśyāmi śūrāṇāṃ raṇamūrdhani tat tad vikatthamānānāṃ bhāraṃ codvahatāṃ mṛdhe
english: I see no fault in this — that heroes, at the head of battle, should boast in one way or another while they bear up the burden of the fight.

sanskrit: yaṃ bhāraṃ puruṣo voḍhuṃ manasā hi vyavasyati daivam asya dhruvaṃ tatra sāhāyyāyopapadyate
english: Whatever burden a man resolves in his mind to carry, fate surely comes to his aid in that undertaking.

sanskrit: vyavasāyadvitīyo 'haṃ manasā bhāram udvahan garjāmi yady ahaṃ vipra tava kiṃ tatra naśyati
english: If I, having resolve for my companion, bear up the burden in my mind and roar, O brahmin, what of yours is lost thereby?

sanskrit: vṛthā śūrā na garjanti sajalā iva toyadāḥ sāmarthyam ātmano jñātvā tato garjanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: Heroes do not roar in vain, like rain clouds laden with water; the wise roar only after knowing their own strength.

sanskrit: so 'ham adya raṇe yattaḥ sahitau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau utsahe tarasā jetuṃ tato garjāmi gautama
english: And so today, braced for battle, I am eager to conquer by my swiftness both Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava united; that is why I roar, O Gautama.

sanskrit: paśya tvaṃ garjitasyāsya phalaṃ me vipra sānugaḥ hatvā pāṇḍusutān ājau sahakṛṣṇān sasātvatān duryodhanāya dāsyāmi pṛthivīṃ hatakaṇṭakām
english: Behold, O brahmin, with your followers, the fruit of this roaring of mine: having slain the sons of Pāṇḍu in battle, together with Kṛṣṇa and the Sātvatas, I shall give to Duryodhana an earth cleansed of its thorns.

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca manorathapralāpo me na grāhyas tava sūtaja yadā kṣipasi vai kṛṣṇau dharmarājaṃ ca pāṇḍavam
english: Kṛpa said: I cannot accept this babbling of your daydreams, O son of a sūta, when you would hurl yourself against the two Kṛṣṇas and the Pāṇḍava, the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: dhruvas tatra jayaḥ karṇa yatra yuddhaviśāradau devagandharvayakṣāṇāṃ manuṣyoragarakṣasām daṃśitānām api raṇe ajeyau kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: There victory is certain, Karṇa, where stand those two masters of war; even when arrayed for battle, the two Kṛṣṇas and the Pāṇḍava are unconquerable by gods, gandharvas, yakṣas, men, serpents, and rākṣasas.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaḥ satyavāg dānto gurudaivatapūjakaḥ nityaṃ dharmarataś caiva kṛtāstraś ca viśeṣataḥ dhṛtimāṃś ca kṛtajñaś ca dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Devoted to the brahmins, truthful in speech, self-controlled, a worshipper of teachers and gods, ever delighting in dharma, and above all skilled in arms, steadfast and grateful — such is Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: bhrātaraś cāsya balinaḥ sarvāstreṣu kṛtaśramāḥ guruvṛttiratāḥ prājñā dharmanityā yaśasvinaḥ
english: And his brothers are mighty, practised in every weapon, devoted to the service of their elders, wise, ever true to dharma, and renowned.

sanskrit: saṃbandhinaś cendravīryāḥ svanuraktāḥ prahāriṇaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca daurmukhir janamejayaḥ
english: Their kinsmen too are valiant as Indra, loyal, and skilled in striking — Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the son of Durmukha, and Janamejaya;

sanskrit: candraseno bhadrasenaḥ kīrtidharmā dhruvo dharaḥ vasucandro dāmacandraḥ siṃhacandraḥ suvedhanaḥ
english: Candrasena, Bhadrasena, Kīrtidharman, Dhruva, Dhara, Vasucandra, Dāmacandra, Siṃhacandra, and Suvedhana;

sanskrit: drupadasya tathā putrā drupadaś ca mahāstravit yeṣām arthāya saṃyatto matsyarājaḥ sahānugaḥ
english: and likewise the sons of Drupada, and Drupada himself, knower of the great weapons, for whose cause the king of the Matsyas with his followers stands ready;

sanskrit: śatānīkaḥ sudaśanaḥ śrutānīkaḥ śrutadhvajaḥ balānīko jayānīko jayāśvo rathavāhanaḥ
english: Śatānīka, Sudarśana, Śrutānīka, Śrutadhvaja, Balānīka, Jayānīka, Jayāśva, and Rathavāhana;

sanskrit: candrodayaḥ kāmaratho virāṭabhrātaraḥ śubhāḥ yamau ca draupadeyāś ca rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ yeṣām arthāya yudhyante na teṣāṃ vidyate kṣayaḥ
english: Candrodaya and Kāmaratha, the noble brothers of Virāṭa, the twins, the sons of Draupadī, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca — for those in whose cause these fight, there is no destruction.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ khalu jagat sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānavam sayakṣarākṣasagaṇaṃ sabhūtabhujagadvipam niḥśeṣam astravīryeṇa kuryātāṃ bhīmaphalgunau
english: Truly, if they wished, Bhīma and Phalguna could by the power of their weapons make an utter end of the whole world — with its gods, asuras, and men, its hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas, its spirits, serpents, and elephants.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraś ca pṛthivīṃ nirdahed ghoracakṣuṣā aprameyabalaḥ śaurir yeṣām arthe ca daṃśitaḥ kathaṃ tān saṃyuge karṇa jetum utsahase parān
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira could burn up the earth with his terrible glance; while Śauri of immeasurable strength stands armed for their cause — how then, Karṇa, do you presume to conquer those foes in battle?

sanskrit: mahān apanayas tv eṣa tava nityaṃ hi sūtaja yas tvam utsahase yoddhuṃ samare śauriṇā saha
english: This is ever a great folly of yours, O son of a sūta — that you should presume to fight in battle against Śauri.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktas tu rādheyaḥ prahasan bharatarṣabha abravīc ca tadā karṇo guruṃ śāradvataṃ kṛpam
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed, O bull of the Bhāratas, the son of Rādhā laughed aloud, and then Karṇa spoke to the teacher, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: satyam uktaṃ tvayā brahman pāṇḍavān prati yad vacaḥ ete cānye ca bahavo guṇāḥ pāṇḍusuteṣu vai
english: True are the words you have spoken, O brahmin, concerning the Pāṇḍavas; these and many other virtues do indeed dwell in the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: ajayyāś ca raṇe pārthā devair api savāsavaiḥ sadaityayakṣagandharvapiśācoragarākṣasaiḥ tathāpi pārthāñ jeṣyāmi śaktyā vāsavadattayā
english: The Pārthas are unconquerable in battle even by the gods led by Vāsava, with the daityas, yakṣas, gandharvas, piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas; yet still I shall conquer the Pārthas with the dart given me by Vāsava.

sanskrit: mamāpy amoghā datteyaṃ śaktiḥ śakreṇa vai dvija etayā nihaniṣyāmi savyasācinam āhave
english: This unfailing dart was given to me by Śakra, O brahmin; with it I shall strike down Savyasācin in the fray.

sanskrit: hate tu pāṇḍave kṛṣṇo bhrātaraś cāsya sodarāḥ anarjunā na śakṣyanti mahīṃ bhoktuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: And once that Pāṇḍava is slain, Kṛṣṇa and his own brothers, bereft of Arjuna, will in no wise be able to enjoy the earth.

sanskrit: teṣu naṣṭeṣu sarveṣu pṛthivīyaṃ sasāgarā ayatnāt kauraveyasya vaśe sthāsyati gautama
english: And when all of them have perished, this earth with her oceans will, without effort, fall under the sway of the son of Kuru, O Gautama.

sanskrit: sunītair iha sarvārthāḥ sidhyante nātra saṃśayaḥ etam artham ahaṃ jñātvā tato garjāmi gautama
english: By sound policy all aims are accomplished here — of that there is no doubt; knowing this purpose, I roar accordingly, O Gautama.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu vṛddhaś ca vipraś ca aśaktaś cāpi saṃyuge kṛtasnehaś ca pārtheṣu mohān mām avamanyase
english: But you are old, and a brahmin, and unable in battle, and besides you bear affection for the Pārthas; out of folly you despise me.

sanskrit: yady evaṃ vakṣyase bhūyo mām apriyam iha dvija tatas te khaḍgam udyamya jihvāṃ chetsyāmi durmate
english: If you speak to me again in this unwelcome way, O brahmin, then, raising my sword, I will cut out your tongue, you fool.

sanskrit: yac cāpi pāṇḍavān vipra stotum icchasi saṃyuge bhīṣayan sarvasainyāni kauraveyāṇi durmate atrāpi śṛṇu me vākyaṃ yathāvad gadato dvija
english: And as for your wishing to extol the Pāṇḍavas in this battle, O brahmin, frightening all the Kaurava armies, you fool — hear too my words on this, as I rightly speak them, O twice-born.

sanskrit: duryodhanaś ca droṇaś ca śakunir durmukho jayaḥ duḥśāsano vṛṣaseno madrarājas tvam eva ca somadattaś ca bhūriś ca tathā drauṇir viviṃśatiḥ
english: Duryodhana and Droṇa, Śakuni, Durmukha, Jaya, Duḥśāsana, Vṛṣasena, the king of the Madras, and you yourself, Somadatta and Bhūri, and likewise Aśvatthāman and Viviṃśati —

sanskrit: tiṣṭheyur daṃśitā yatra sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ jayed etān raṇe ko nu śakratulyabalo 'py ariḥ
english: where all these masters of war stand arrayed for battle, what foe, even one equal in might to Śakra, could conquer them in the fray?

sanskrit: śūrāś ca hi kṛtāstrāś ca balinaḥ svargalipsavaḥ dharmajñā yuddhakuśalā hanyur yuddhe surān api
english: For these heroes, skilled in arms, mighty, longing for heaven, knowers of dharma and adept in war, could slay even the gods in battle.

sanskrit: ete sthāsyanti saṃgrāme pāṇḍavānāṃ vadhārthinaḥ jayam ākāṅkṣamāṇā hi kauraveyasya daṃśitāḥ
english: These will stand in the battle, seeking the slaughter of the Pāṇḍavas, arrayed and longing for the victory of the son of Kuru.

sanskrit: daivāyattam ahaṃ manye jayaṃ subalinām api yatra bhīṣmo mahābāhuḥ śete śaraśatācitaḥ
english: I hold that victory rests with fate, even for the most mighty — for there lies Bhīṣma of the great arms, covered with a hundred arrows.

sanskrit: vikarṇaś citrasenaś ca bāhlīko 'tha jayadrathaḥ bhūriśravā jayaś caiva jalasaṃdhaḥ sudakṣiṇaḥ
english: Vikarṇa and Citrasena, Bāhlika and Jayadratha, Bhūriśravas and Jaya, Jalasaṃdha and Sudakṣiṇa,

sanskrit: śalaś ca rathināṃ śreṣṭho bhagadattaś ca vīryavān ete cānye ca rājāno devair api sudurjayāḥ
english: and Śala, foremost among chariot-warriors, and the valiant Bhagadatta — these and other kings, hard to conquer even by the gods,

sanskrit: nihatāḥ samare śūrāḥ pāṇḍavair balavattarāḥ kim anyad daivasaṃyogān manyase puruṣādhama
english: these heroes, mightier still, have been slain in battle by the Pāṇḍavas. What else but the working of fate do you suppose it, O basest of men?

sanskrit: yāṃś ca tān stauṣi satataṃ duryodhanaripūn dvija teṣām api hatāḥ śūrāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And those foes of Duryodhana whom you ceaselessly praise, O brahmin — of them too the heroes have been slain by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: kṣīyante sarvasainyāni kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha prabhāvaṃ nātra paśyāmi pāṇḍavānāṃ kathaṃ cana
english: The whole armies of the Kurus are wasting away together with the Pāṇḍavas; in this I see no special might of the Pāṇḍavas at all.

sanskrit: yāṃs tān balavato nityaṃ manyase tvaṃ dvijādhama yatiṣye 'haṃ yathāśakti yoddhuṃ taiḥ saha saṃyuge duryodhanahitārthāya jayo daive pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Those whom you ever deem so mighty, O basest of brahmins — I will strive with all my strength to fight against them in battle. For the welfare of Duryodhana I shall fight; but victory rests with fate.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā paruṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sūtaputreṇa mātulam khaḍgam udyamya vegena drauṇir abhyapatad drutam
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing his maternal uncle thus harshly reviled by the son of the sūta, Aśvatthāman, raising his sword, rushed swiftly upon him in a fury.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca karṇa paśya sudurbuddhe tiṣṭhedānīṃ narādhama eṣa te 'dya śiraḥ kāyād uddharāmi sudurmate
english: Aśvatthāman said: Look here, Karṇa, you of wretched mind! Stand fast now, basest of men — this day I shall lift your head from your body, you utter fool.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tam utpatantaṃ vegena rājā duryodhanaḥ svayam nyavārayan mahārāja kṛpaś ca dvipadāṃ varaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As he sprang up in his fury, O great king, King Duryodhana himself restrained him, and so did Kṛpa, foremost of men.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca śūro 'yaṃ samaraślāghī durmatiś ca dvijādhamaḥ āsādayatu madvīryaṃ muñcemaṃ kurusattama
english: Karṇa said: This brahmin is a hero, a boaster in battle, and dull of wit, the basest of his kind — let him come up against my prowess; release him, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmovāca tavaitat kṣamyate 'smābhiḥ sūtātmaja sudurmate darpam utsiktam etat te phalguno nāśayiṣyati
english: Aśvatthāman said: This of yours we forgive, O son of a sūta, you utter fool; but this overweening arrogance of yours Phalguna will destroy.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca aśvatthāman prasīdasva kṣantum arhasi mānada kopaḥ khalu na kartavyaḥ sūtaputre kathaṃ cana
english: Duryodhana said: Aśvatthāman, be appeased; you ought to forgive, O bestower of honour. No anger at all should be shown toward the son of the sūta.

sanskrit: tvayi karṇe kṛpe droṇe madrarāje 'tha saubale mahat kāryaṃ samāyattaṃ prasīda dvijasattama
english: Upon you, upon Karṇa, Kṛpa, Droṇa, the king of the Madras, and the son of Subala rests our great task; be appeased, O best of brahmins.

sanskrit: ete hy abhimukhāḥ sarve rādheyena yuyutsavaḥ āyānti pāṇḍavā brahmann āhvayantaḥ samantataḥ
english: For lo, all these Pāṇḍavas, eager to fight against the son of Rādhā, are advancing toward us, O brahmin, challenging us on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇo 'pi rathināṃ śreṣṭhaś cāpam udyamya vīryavān kauravāgryaiḥ parivṛtaḥ śakro devagaṇair iva paryatiṣṭhata tejasvī svabāhubalam āśritaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: And Karṇa too, foremost of chariot-warriors, the valiant one, raising his bow and surrounded by the chief Kauravas as Śakra by the hosts of gods, took his stand, blazing with splendour and relying on the strength of his own arms.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ karṇasya saha pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃrabdhasya mahārāja siṃhanādavināditam
english: Then began the battle of the enraged Karṇa with the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, resounding with the roars of lions.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavā rājan pāñcālāś ca yaśasvinaḥ dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ mahābāhum uccaiḥ śabdam athānadan
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, O king, and the renowned Pāñcālas, seeing Karṇa of the mighty arms, raised a loud cry.

sanskrit: ayaṃ karṇaḥ kutaḥ karṇas tiṣṭha karṇa mahāraṇe yudhyasva sahito 'smābhir durātman puruṣādhama
english: "Here is Karṇa! Where now is Karṇa? Stand, Karṇa, in this great battle! Fight against us, you wicked-souled, basest of men!"

sanskrit: anye tu dṛṣṭvā rādheyaṃ krodharaktekṣaṇābruvan hanyatām ayam utsiktaḥ sūtaputro 'lpacetanaḥ
english: And others, seeing the son of Rādhā, their eyes red with rage, said: "Let this arrogant, dull-witted son of the sūta be slain!"

sanskrit: sarvaiḥ pārthivaśārdūlair nānenārtho 'sti jīvatā atyantavairī pārthānāṃ satataṃ pāpapūruṣaḥ
english: "There is no use for all you tigers among kings in his living; this wicked man is the unending, ceaseless foe of the Pārthas."

sanskrit: eṣa mūlaṃ hy anarthānāṃ duryodhanamate sthitaḥ hatainam iti jalpantaḥ kṣatriyāḥ samupādravan
english: "For he is the very root of our calamities, planted firm in Duryodhana's counsel — slay him!" So crying, the kṣatriyas rushed upon him together.

sanskrit: mahatā śaravarṣeṇa chādayanto mahārathāḥ vadhārthaṃ sūtaputrasya pāṇḍaveyena coditāḥ
english: With a great shower of arrows the mighty chariot-warriors, urged on by the Pāṇḍava, covered him over, seeking the death of the son of the sūta.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvāṃs tathā dṛṣṭvā dhāvamānān mahārathān na vivyathe sūtaputro na ca trāsam agacchata
english: But seeing all those great chariot-warriors thus rushing on, the son of the sūta neither faltered nor gave way to fear.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā nagarakalpaṃ tam uddhūtaṃ sainyasāgaram piprīṣus tava putrāṇāṃ saṃgrāmeṣv aparājitaḥ
english: Beholding that surging ocean of an army, vast as a city, he who was unvanquished in battles sought to bring cheer to your sons.

sanskrit: sāyakaughena balavān kṣiprakārī mahābalaḥ vārayām āsa tat sainyaṃ samantād bharatarṣabha
english: The strong one, swift in action and of great might, held back that army on every side with a flood of arrows, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tatas tu śaravarṣeṇa pārthivās tam avārayan dhanūṃṣi te vidhunvānāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ ayodhayanta rādheyaṃ śakraṃ daityagaṇā iva
english: Then the kings checked him with a rain of arrows, shaking their bows by hundreds and by thousands; they did battle with the son of Rādhā as the hosts of daityas with Śakra.

sanskrit: śaravarṣaṃ tu tat karṇaḥ pārthivaiḥ samudīritam śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samantād vyakirat prabho
english: But that rain of arrows loosed by the kings Karṇa scattered on every side with a mighty rain of arrows of his own, O lord.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavat teṣāṃ kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇām yathā devāsure yuddhe śakrasya saha dānavaiḥ
english: That battle of theirs, each seeking to repay blow with counter-blow, became like the battle of Śakra with the dānavas in the war of gods and asuras.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma sūtaputrasya lāghavam yad enaṃ samare yattā nāpnuvanta pare yudhi
english: There we beheld the marvellous swiftness of the son of the sūta — that even striving in battle, his foes could not reach him in the fight.

sanskrit: nivārya ca śaraughāṃs tān pārthivānāṃ mahārathaḥ yugeṣv īṣāsu chatreṣu dhvajeṣu ca hayeṣu ca ātmanāmāṅkitān bāṇān rādheyaḥ prāhiṇoc chitān
english: Warding off those floods of arrows from the kings, the great chariot-warrior, son of Rādhā, sent forth keen shafts marked with his own name into their yokes and chariot-poles, their parasols and banners and horses.

sanskrit: tatas te vyākulībhūtā rājānaḥ karṇapīḍitāḥ babhramus tatra tatraiva gāvaḥ śītārditā iva
english: Then those kings, thrown into confusion and sorely pressed by Karṇa, wandered hither and thither, like cattle tormented by the cold.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ vadhyamānānāṃ gajānāṃ rathināṃ tathā tatra tatrābhyavekṣāmaḥ saṃghān karṇena pātitān
english: Here and there we looked upon throngs of horses, elephants, and chariot-warriors being slaughtered, struck down by Karṇa.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ patitai rājan bāhubhiś ca samantataḥ āstīrṇā vasudhā sarvā śūrāṇām anivartinām
english: With heads fallen, O king, and with arms strewn on every side, the whole earth was carpeted with those of heroes who never turned back.

sanskrit: hataiś ca hanyamānaiś ca niṣṭanadbhiś ca sarvaśaḥ babhūvāyodhanaṃ raudraṃ vaivasvatapuropamam
english: With the slain and the dying and those groaning on every side, the battlefield grew terrible, like the city of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam aśvatthāmānam āsādya tadā vākyam uvāca ha
english: Then King Duryodhana, beholding the prowess of Karṇa, approached Aśvatthāman and spoke these words.

sanskrit: yudhyate 'sau raṇe karṇo daṃśitaḥ sarvapārthivaiḥ paśyaitāṃ dravatīṃ senāṃ karṇasāyakapīḍitām kārttikeyena vidhvastām āsurīṃ pṛtanām iva
english: "Yonder Karṇa, arrayed for battle, fights against all the kings; behold this army fleeing, sore pressed by the arrows of Karṇa, like the demonic host shattered by Kārttikeya."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaitāṃ nirjitāṃ senāṃ raṇe karṇena dhīmatā abhiyāty eṣa bībhatsuḥ sūtaputrajighāṃsayā
english: "Seeing this army vanquished in battle by the wise Karṇa, here comes Bībhatsu, longing to slay the son of the sūta."

sanskrit: tad yathā paśyamānānāṃ sūtaputraṃ mahāratham na hanyāt pāṇḍavaḥ saṃkhye tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: "So let such measures be devised that, before our very eyes, the Pāṇḍava may not slay the great chariot-warrior, the son of the sūta, in this battle."

sanskrit: tato drauṇiḥ kṛpaḥ śalyo hārdikyaś ca mahārathaḥ pratyudyayus tadā pārthaṃ sūtaputraparīpsayā
english: Then Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, Śalya, and the great chariot-warrior the son of Hṛdika went forth against Pārtha, seeking to protect the son of the sūta.

sanskrit: āyāntaṃ dṛśya kaunteyaṃ vṛtraṃ devacamūm iva pratyudyayau tadā karṇo yathā śakraḥ pratāpavān
english: Seeing the son of Kuntī advancing like Vṛtra against the army of the gods, Karṇa then went forth to meet him, glorious as Śakra.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃrabdhaṃ phalgunaṃ dṛṣṭvā kālāntakayamopamam karṇo vaikartanaḥ sūta pratyapadyat kim uttaram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Seeing the enraged Phalguna, like Yama the all-ending at the world's close, what response, O sūta, did Karṇa Vaikartana make?

sanskrit: sa hy aspardhata pārthena nityam eva mahārathaḥ āśaṃsate ca bībhatsuṃ yuddhe jetuṃ sudāruṇe
english: For that great chariot-warrior ever vied with Pārtha, and hoped to conquer Bībhatsu in dreadful battle.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ sahasā prāptaṃ nityam atyantavairiṇam karṇo vaikartanaḥ sūta kim uttaram apadyata
english: What response, then, O sūta, did Karṇa Vaikartana make to that unending enemy, now suddenly come upon him?
